The HR/LR labels come from one outcome chosen in advance. Clustering asks the data instead: if
people are grouped by how they responded, do natural groups appear? This walkthrough runs for three
groupings, set by the `grouping` parameter:

| grouping | people clustered on |
|---|---|
| `Muscle_size` | % change over training in fibre area (mixed, type I, type II) and muscle area |
| `Muscle_strength` | % change over training in leg-press and leg-extension 1RM |
| `Proteome` | the module eigengenes, separately at T1, T2, T3, over training and after the bout |

No step here reads a protein contrast.

## Packages

cluster supplies PAM and the gap statistic; fpc the bootstrap stability; mclust the adjusted Rand
index. fpc and mclust are called with `::`.

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)
library(cluster)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "analysis_reporting_helpers.R"))
params$grouping
```

## What gets clustered

Each grouping becomes one or more people-by-feature matrices. Every feature is z-scored (centred
and divided by its standard deviation) so no trait or module dominates by its scale. People missing
any feature are left out of that matrix.

```{r}
#| label: inputs
is_proteome <- params$grouping == "Proteome"
out <- here("02_Groups", params$grouping, "c_data")
dir.create(out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
inputs <- c(
  modules = if (is_proteome) "01_Processing/06_Module_Building/c_data/modules.rds",
  phenotype = "00_Setup/Input/phenotype.csv"
)
paths <- map_chr(inputs, here)
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
phenotype <- readr::read_csv(paths[["phenotype"]], show_col_types = FALSE)
arm_of <- set_names(phenotype$arm, phenotype$subject)
```

For the two phenotype groupings the features are the training % changes of the chosen traits.

```{r}
#| label: phenotype-matrix
#| eval: !expr '!is_proteome'
traits <- list(
  Muscle_size = c("pct_fcsa_mixed", "pct_fcsa_type1", "pct_fcsa_type2", "pct_mcsa"),
  Muscle_strength = c("pct_leg_press_1rm", "pct_leg_ext_1rm")
)[[params$grouping]]
change <- phenotype_tables(phenotype)$pairings$training
complete <- change |>
  select(subject, all_of(traits)) |>
  drop_na()
x <- scale(as.matrix(select(complete, -subject)))
rownames(x) <- complete$subject
matrices <- set_names(list(x), params$grouping)
head(round(x, 2), 4)
```

For the proteome the features are the 15 module eigengenes, as levels at each time point and as
within-person change over training (T2 − T1) and after the bout (T3 − T2).

```{r}
#| label: proteome-matrices
#| eval: !expr is_proteome
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "proteome_inputs.R"))
modules <- readRDS(paths[["modules"]])
meta <- as_tibble(modules$meta)
values <- modules$eigengenes
matrices <- list(
  T1 = values_at_timepoint(values, meta, "T1"), T2 = values_at_timepoint(values, meta, "T2"),
  T3 = values_at_timepoint(values, meta, "T3"),
  training = within_subject_change(values, meta, "T1", "T2"),
  acute = within_subject_change(values, meta, "T2", "T3")
) |>
  map(\(m) scale(t(m)))
stopifnot(identical(names(matrices), inputs_used))
map(matrices, dim)
```

## How many groups

PAM (partitioning around medoids) picks K real people as group centres and assigns everyone to the
nearest centre. PAM always returns K groups, so three diagnostics judge whether they are real:

- Gap statistic (Tibshirani, Walther and Hastie 2001): compares how tight the K groups are with
  how tight they would be in 500 reference data sets with no group structure. The one-standard-error
  rule (`maxSE(method = "Tibs2001SEmax")`) picks the smallest K whose gap is within one standard
  error of the best. K = 1, no groups, is a possible answer.
- Mean silhouette: how much closer people sit to their own group than to the next, from −1 to 1.
- Bootstrap Jaccard (Hennig 2007, `fpc::clusterboot`, 500 resamples): how often each group comes
  back when people are resampled. Hennig reads 0.75 or more as stable, 0.6 to 0.75 as doubtful and
  below 0.6 as not to be trusted.

The adjusted Rand index (ARI) against HR/LR describes agreement with the study's labels; 0 is
chance agreement, 1 identical. It decides nothing.

`cluster_people()` takes one z-scored matrix and returns the gap table, the K the gap statistic
picks, the PAM fits for K = 2 and 3, their stability, and the diagnostics table. It is applied to
each matrix of the grouping.

```{r}
#| label: cluster-people
pam1 <- \(x, k) list(cluster = pam(x, k, cluster.only = TRUE))
cluster_people <- function(x, k_max = 3, n_boot = 500) {
  set.seed(1)
  gap <- clusGap(x, FUNcluster = pam1, K.max = k_max, B = n_boot)
  gap_table <- as_tibble(gap$Tab) |> mutate(k = seq_len(n()), .before = 1)
  k_gap <- maxSE(gap_table$gap, gap_table$SE.sim, method = "Tibs2001SEmax")
  solutions <- map(set_names(2:k_max), \(k) pam(x, k))
  stability <- map(set_names(2:k_max), \(k) {
    boot <- fpc::clusterboot(x,
      B = n_boot, clustermethod = fpc::claraCBI, k = k, usepam = TRUE,
      seed = 1, count = FALSE
    )
    tibble(k = k, cluster = seq_along(boot$bootmean), jaccard = boot$bootmean)
  }) |>
    list_rbind()
  diagnostics <- gap_table |>
    left_join(
      imap(solutions, \(fit, k) {
        tibble(
          k = as.integer(k), mean_silhouette = fit$silinfo$avg.width,
          sizes = paste(table(fit$clustering), collapse = "/"),
          hr_lr_ari = mclust::adjustedRandIndex(fit$clustering, arm_of[rownames(x)])
        )
      }) |>
        list_rbind(),
      by = "k"
    ) |>
    left_join(
      summarise(stability,
        min_jaccard = min(jaccard), jaccard = paste(round(jaccard, 2), collapse = "/"), .by = k
      ),
      by = "k"
    )
  list(
    gap_table = gap_table, k_gap = k_gap, solutions = solutions, stability = stability,
    diagnostics = diagnostics, pcs = prcomp(x)
  )
}
fits <- map(matrices, cluster_people)
map(fits, \(fit) select(fit$diagnostics, k, gap, SE.sim, mean_silhouette, sizes, jaccard))
```

## K = 1, and K = 2 by decision

The gap statistic picks K = `r paste(unique(map_int(fits, "k_gap")), collapse = " or ")` here
(`r paste(names(fits), map_int(fits, "k_gap"), sep = ": ", collapse = "; ")`). K = 1 means
the data show no natural groups, and that is a result in its own right. K = 2 is then imposed by decision (decisions log, 2026-10-06) so the
exploratory comparisons can ask what separates the two halves the data suggest. Every result
downstream of an imposed split is exploratory; read each split with its bootstrap Jaccard.

```{r}
#| label: choice
imposed_k <- 2L
imposed_reason <- list(
  Muscle_size = paste(
    "Gap statistic selects K = 1; K = 2 imposed by decision (2026-10-06). It reproduces the HR/LR",
    "split exactly, so this grouping repeats that comparison under a size-cluster label."
  ),
  Muscle_strength = paste(
    "Gap statistic selects K = 1; K = 2 imposed by decision (2026-10-06) because both clusters",
    "are stable (bootstrap Jaccard >= 0.84) and the split is independent of HR/LR. Exploratory."
  ),
  Proteome = paste(
    "Gap statistic selects K = 1 at every input, which is reported as the result; K = 2 imposed",
    "by decision (2026-10-06) so the exploratory grouping can compare the two halves the proteome",
    "suggests. Read each split with its bootstrap Jaccard."
  )
)[[params$grouping]]
k_used <- map_int(fits, \(fit) coalesce(imposed_k, fit$k_gap))
stopifnot(k_used == 2)
map_int(fits, "k_gap")
```

## Groups and tables

The phenotype groupings name their two groups `Hi` and `Lo` by the mean of the first trait. The
proteome groups keep PAM's numbering, `C1` and `C2`; the number carries no meaning. The traits a
phenotype grouping was built on stay out of its group-by-trait tests; for `Muscle_size` so does
the composite, since these clusters reproduce HR/LR.

```{r}
#| label: phenotype-tables
#| eval: !expr '!is_proteome'
fit <- fits[[1]]
choice <- tibble(
  family = params$grouping,
  n_subjects = nrow(x), traits = paste(traits, collapse = ", "),
  k_gap = fit$k_gap, k_imposed = imposed_k, imposed_reason, k_used = k_used[[1]],
  grouped = k_used[[1]] > 1
)
assignments <- complete |>
  mutate(
    k2 = fit$solutions[["2"]]$clustering, k3 = fit$solutions[["3"]]$clustering,
    cluster = fit$solutions[[as.character(k_used[[1]])]]$clustering
  ) |>
  right_join(select(change, subject), by = "subject") |>
  arrange(cluster, subject)
label_of <- assignments |>
  filter(!is.na(cluster)) |>
  summarise(lead = mean(.data[[traits[1]]]), .by = cluster) |>
  mutate(label = if_else(lead == max(lead), "Hi", "Lo")) |>
  select(cluster, label)
group_of <- assignments |>
  inner_join(label_of, by = "cluster") |>
  with(set_names(label, subject))
defining_traits <- if (params$grouping == "Muscle_size") c(traits, "comp_hypertrophy") else traits
saveRDS(
  list(group_of = group_of, arms = c("Hi", "Lo"), defining_traits = defining_traits),
  file.path(out, "groups.rds")
)
sheets <- list(
  choice = choice, diagnostics = fit$diagnostics, stability = fit$stability,
  assignments = assignments,
  space = as_tibble(fit$pcs$x[, 1:2], rownames = "subject") |>
    left_join(select(assignments, subject, cluster), by = "subject") |>
    mutate(arm = arm_of[subject], group = unname(group_of[subject]), .after = subject),
  space_variance = tibble(
    component = c("PC1", "PC2"), variance_explained = summary(fit$pcs)$importance[2, 1:2]
  )
)
table(group = group_of, hr_lr = arm_of[names(group_of)])
```

```{r}
#| label: proteome-tables
#| eval: !expr is_proteome
per_input <- imap(fits, \(fit, input) {
  x <- matrices[[input]]
  k <- k_used[[input]]
  cluster <- fit$solutions[[as.character(k)]]$clustering
  list(
    choice = tibble(
      input,
      n_subjects = nrow(x), n_features = ncol(x), k_gap = fit$k_gap, k_imposed = imposed_k,
      imposed_reason, k_used = k, grouped = k > 1
    ),
    diagnostics = mutate(fit$diagnostics, input = input, .before = 1),
    stability = mutate(fit$stability, input = input, .before = 1),
    assignments = tibble(
      input,
      subject = rownames(x), arm = unname(arm_of[rownames(x)]),
      k2 = fit$solutions[["2"]]$clustering, k3 = fit$solutions[["3"]]$clustering, cluster
    ),
    space = tibble(
      input,
      subject = rownames(x), arm = unname(arm_of[rownames(x)]),
      cluster, PC1 = fit$pcs$x[, 1], PC2 = fit$pcs$x[, 2]
    ),
    space_variance = tibble(
      input,
      component = c("PC1", "PC2"), variance_explained = summary(fit$pcs)$importance[2, 1:2]
    )
  )
})
sheets <- map(set_names(names(per_input[[1]])), \(sheet) list_rbind(map(per_input, sheet)))
dir.create(file.path(out, "groups"), showWarnings = FALSE)
walk(inputs_used, \(input) {
  used <- filter(sheets$assignments, input == .env$input)
  saveRDS(
    list(
      group_of = set_names(paste0("C", used$cluster), used$subject),
      arms = c("C1", "C2"), defining_traits = character(0)
    ),
    file.path(out, "groups", paste0(input, ".rds"))
  )
})
count(sheets$assignments, input, cluster, arm)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-gap
#| fig-cap: "Gap statistic by K, ± one standard error. Dashed: the K the one-SE rule picks."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3
imap(fits, \(fit, input) mutate(fit$gap_table, input = input, k_gap = fit$k_gap)) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  ggplot(aes(k, gap)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = gap - SE.sim, ymax = gap + SE.sim)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = k_gap), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~input, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:3) +
  labs(x = "K", y = "gap") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-space
#| fig-cap: "People on the first two principal components of what they were clustered on."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.5
sheets$space |>
  mutate(input = if (is_proteome) input else params$grouping) |>
  ggplot(aes(PC1, PC2, colour = factor(cluster), shape = arm)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~input, nrow = 1) +
  labs(colour = "cluster", shape = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)
```

## Validation

```{r}
#| label: validate
stopifnot(
  all(map_lgl(fits, \(fit) fit$k_gap %in% 1:3)),
  all(sheets$stability$jaccard >= 0 & sheets$stability$jaccard <= 1),
  !anyNA(sheets$space$cluster[!is.na(sheets$space$PC1)])
)
```

## Summary

The gap statistic picks K = `r paste(unique(map_int(fits, "k_gap")), collapse = " or ")` for
`r params$grouping`. The imposed K = 2 split has bootstrap Jaccard
`r paste(sprintf("%.2f", range(filter(sheets$stability, k == 2)$jaccard)), collapse = " to ")`
across its groups and matrices; `r sum(filter(sheets$stability, k == 2)$jaccard < 0.6)` of
`r nrow(filter(sheets$stability, k == 2))` groups fall below 0.6, Hennig's line for a group not
to be trusted.

## Save

```{r}
#| label: save
holds <- if (is_proteome) {
  c(
    "Per input: subjects, features, K selected by the gap statistic, any imposed K and reason.",
    "Per input and K: gap, SE, mean silhouette, sizes, HR/LR adjusted Rand index, Jaccard.",
    "Per input, K and cluster: mean bootstrap Jaccard (fpc::clusterboot, PAM).",
    "Per input and subject: HR/LR (for description), the K = 2 and K = 3 clusters, cluster used.",
    "Per input and subject: HR/LR, cluster, and PC1 and PC2 of the z-scored eigengenes.",
    "Per input: share of variance on PC1 and PC2 of the z-scored eigengenes."
  )
} else {
  c(
    "K selected by the gap statistic, any imposed K and its reason, and the K used downstream.",
    "Per K: gap, SE, mean silhouette, group sizes, HR/LR adjusted Rand index, bootstrap Jaccard.",
    "Per K and cluster: mean bootstrap Jaccard (fpc::clusterboot, PAM).",
    "Per subject: the traits, the K = 2 and K = 3 clusters, and the cluster used downstream.",
    "Per subject: HR/LR arm, group, cluster, and PC1 and PC2 of the scaled traits.",
    "Share of variance on PC1 and PC2 of the scaled traits."
  )
}
write_workbook(
  sheets[c("choice", "diagnostics", "stability", "assignments", "space", "space_variance")],
  holds, file.path(out, "clustering.xlsx"), inputs, paths
)
```
